title: Heuristics
summary: Every signal the planner computes to rank states: h_FF and its helpful actions, cost and numeric variants, landmarks, novelty, and the admissible stack for optimal mode.
body: The satisficing side is built on one heuristic — FF's relaxed plan over a numeric-interval relaxation — plus three cheaper second signals (helpful actions, landmark count, novelty) that change the order of search rather than estimate distance. The optimal side has its own admissible stack (hmax, LM-cut, incremental LM-cut) with the numeric layer bound maxed in. Everything is deterministic and thread-count independent: heuristic values are pure functions of the state, and parallelism only changes when they are computed.

children.title: FF heuristic (h_FF)
children.summary: The workhorse: delete-relaxed planning graph with numeric intervals, greedy relaxed-plan extraction, helpful actions. Every satisficing rung evaluates it.
children.body:
heuristic.rs is the single satisficing heuristic of ferroplan. Every satisficing search — EHC, LAMA, weighted best-first, the cost sweep, the partition subplanner, the PDDL3 loops, the temporal pruned pass — calls into it. The design constraint is throughput under parallel evaluation: no allocation on the hot path, a reusable Scratch per worker, CSR task layout, env reads hoisted into Hatches.

The phases of one evaluation are reset → build_rpg → goal check → relaxed_extract. The result is an i32 count or None (relaxed dead end). There is no hadd in the tree: the satisficing side uses hFF only; hmax lives in optimal.rs.

children.title: Delete relaxation (the idea)
children.summary: Ignore every delete effect; facts only accumulate. The length of a plan for that easier task estimates the real distance.
children.body:
Idea. In the delete-relaxed task an action never makes anything false, so applicability is monotone: once an op is applicable it stays applicable. Reachability becomes a fixpoint over a layered planning graph (fact layer 0 = current state, op layer k = ops whose preconditions are all in fact layers ≤ k). The optimal relaxed plan length h+ is a lower bound on the real plan length but is NP-hard to compute; FF instead extracts some relaxed plan greedily and counts its ops (hFF). That count is not admissible (the greedy extraction can over-count shared work, and numeric repetition counting can over-charge) but it is informative, cheap and the de-facto satisficing heuristic since 2001.

In ferroplan. The relaxed graph runs directly over the packed task (PackedTask bitsets and CSR slices: pre_pos, add, cond, achievers(f)). Numeric fluents are relaxed to monotone intervals [lb, ub] that only widen (the Metric-FF treatment). The module doc calls the result "the same algorithm as the (oracle-verified) metricff heuristic". A relaxed dead end (goal never reached at fixpoint) returns None and is a safe prune when the numeric interval audit passes.

children.title: Scratch: allocation-free buffers
children.summary: Per-worker reusable buffers, reset per evaluation by a generation bump instead of clearing arrays.
children.body:
Scratch holds every working array of one evaluation: reached, fact_layer, op_layer, numeric bounds lb/ub, selected, sel_reps, need_fact, the extraction queue, num_applied, cond_ops, the helpful list, and the TRPG-lite fact_time/op_time columns.

A worker thread builds one Scratch per solve (par::par_map_with passes || Scratch::new(task) as the per-worker init). reset() bumps a gen stamp so membership in op_layer/selected/need_fact is "stamp == gen" — O(1) reset instead of 2·n_ops + n_facts writes (this was item 1 of the perf backlog in docs/perf-notes.md). The module doc gives the reason for the design: per-state allocation churn and global-allocator contention across workers was the main limit on raw speed and on parallel scaling.

Hatches caches every FF_NO_NEED_DIRS/FF_NUMPRE_*/FF_NO_CONSUME env read at construction; reading the environment per evaluation cost ~2% of every numeric evaluation in the coins i18 profiles.

children.title: build_rpg: the relaxed planning graph
children.summary: Two-phase incremental layering of facts, ops and numeric intervals until the goal is relaxed-reached, a fixpoint, or LAYER_CAP.
children.body:
build_rpg expands layer by layer. Only unapplied ops are re-scanned each layer (applied ops never lose applicability under the relaxation), except ops with relevant numeric effects (num_applied, re-widened every layer) and ops with conditional effects (cond_ops, whose conditional adds fire once the condition becomes reached). Numeric bounds widen through widen(); only effects on relevant fluents (read by some precondition, goal, or transitively by them) are applied, which is exact and stops irrelevant unbounded growth.

It returns an RpgExit: GoalAt(k), Fixpoint (goal unreachable → h = ∞), or Cap after LAYER_CAP = 2000 rounds. Satisficing callers ignore the exit; the optimal mode uses GoalAt(k) as an admissible length bound. With to_fixpoint it ignores the goal and runs to fixpoint, which reachability_layers uses for landmark extraction.

A note in docs/perf-notes.md records a negative: a scattered precondition trigger index was tried and reverted, because the sequential CSR scan's cache locality wins on shallow graphs.

children.title: Relaxed-plan extraction (h_FF)
children.summary: Backchain from the goals, picking the lowest-layer achiever of each needed fact; h is the number of selected ops (times repetitions).
children.body:
relaxed_extract seeds a queue with the goal facts, then for each needed fact picks an achiever with achiever(): among the ops adding f (the precomputed add-by-fact index task.achievers(f)), the one with the lowest op layer strictly below f's fact layer (the FF "earliest achiever" rule). select() marks the op, adds reps to the count, records it as helpful if it sits at op layer 0, and queues its positive preconditions. If f is reached only through a conditional effect, queue_cond_for also queues that effect's condition facts.

Numeric goals and preconditions are charged via numeric_achiever (see the numeric node), which can select a mover op several times (repetition counting).

Entry points: relaxed_to (any subgoal, time-blind), relaxed (task goal), relaxed_helpful (h plus helpful set), relaxed_costed (h plus selected op costs), relaxed_plan_ops (the selected ops themselves, used by the PDDL3 polish). Each call is reset + build + extract; the three phases are timed into T_RESET/T_BUILD/T_EXTRACT for FF_RES_DEBUG. extraction_need_facts reads out the stamped need-facts for the novelty driver's R set.

Cost per evaluation: O(ops scanned × layers) for the build plus O(relaxed plan size × achievers) for extraction — microseconds on small STRIPS tasks, up to ~8 ms per evaluation on compiled preference tasks (search.rs cites tpp-qualitative i12: 2,464 evals in 19.8 s).

children.title: Helpful actions / preferred ops
children.summary: Relaxed-plan ops applicable in the current state; they prune EHC and boost LAMA and the enriched fallback.
children.body:
Idea. FF observed that the first step of a good real plan is usually among the relaxed plan's layer-0 ops. Restricting or favoring those "helpful actions" collapses the branching factor to roughly the relaxed plan's width. LAMA keeps the same signal as "preferred operators" but uses it only to order (a second, favored open list), not to prune, which keeps search complete.

In ferroplan. select() pushes every selected op whose op_layer == 0 onto Scratch::helpful; relaxed_helpful returns (h, helpful) in deterministic selection order. Consumers:

  • EHC (bfs_improve) expands only helpful ops — incomplete, hence the ladder below it.
  • LAMA rung and the enriched best-first fallback (SearchCfg::pref_ops, default-on since 0.26 F1) put helpful-reached successors into a preferred heap, popping 192 preferred + 64 normal per round.
  • Temporal: helpful_needed_adders is a lax fallback (applicable ops adding any precondition a selected op still needs) for when the strict set filters to nothing — temporal relaxed plans often lead through END ops the agenda fires.

Cost: zero extra over hFF (the list is a by-product of extraction); the satisficing best-first only pays for the Vec when pref_ops is on.

children.title: Numeric handling in h
children.summary: Monotone interval bounds, direction-aware fixpoint test, linear numeric subgoaling with repetition counts, and the consumption charge.
children.body:
Intervals. Each relevant fluent carries [lb, ub]; widen() applies increase/decrease/assign/scale effects monotonically. eval_iv evaluates an expression over intervals and num_sat asks whether a comparison is satisfiable anywhere in them. widen is #[inline(always)] on purpose: an extra parameter in 0.28 made LLVM keep it a call and that cost 43% per evaluation on coins-2026 i18 (7.7 → 11.0 µs).

Need directions. NeedDirs/need_dirs mark which bound of each fluent any goal/precondition can actually use. Before that, a consumable's unread lower bound drifting down counted as "progress" and sent every dead-end evaluation to the 2,000-layer cap; the direction-aware test (computed lazily at NEED_PROBE_LAYER = 16) is exact — h is unchanged — and about 78× faster at proving dead ends on rovers-metric-time shapes (book tuning.md).

Achievers. numeric_achiever handles fluent cmp const; numeric_achiever_linear folds linear expressions through linearize into Σ coeff·fluent + k and charges a mover op ceil(gap/rate) repetitions (the 0.19 "linear numeric subgoaling charge", recorded +52/−1 in STATUS.md). consumption_charge (0.29 Lane 2) bills selected ops' decreases of a stock fluent they read with a lower bound, net of the plan's own increases, and prices any deficit through a synthetic fluent ≥ stock + deficit subgoal.

Repetition counting makes hFF stronger on numeric tasks but further from admissible; the admissible numeric bound is a separate path (next node).

children.title: Admissible numeric layer bound
children.summary: With a passing containment audit, the first goal-satisfiable RPG layer lower-bounds plan length on numeric tasks.
children.body:
admissible_goal_layers runs the same build without extraction and reads RpgExit::GoalAt(k). By induction over widen, layer k's facts and intervals contain every state reachable by a real plan of length ≤ k, so k is an admissible bound on plan length; Fixpoint is a sound prune. No repetition-count shortcut lives here: ceil(gap/rate-now) is inadmissible when a plan can raise the rate first (sailing-wind's velocity assign is cited as the witness).

numeric_interval_audit refuses by name the shapes that break containment: scale-up/down on a relevant fluent (widen is one-sided there), a relevant fluent undefined at init, and monitored/shared-condition trajectory automata. A refused audit means "unarmed" — the bound is simply not used.

Consumer: AstarState::eval in optimal.rs takes max(LM-cut or h^max, layer bound) on numeric tasks (the 0.22 Phase 4 "num arm", gated by num_arm_root).

children.title: TRPG-lite time column
children.summary: On timed builds of temporal tasks, a second field on the same RPG loop tracks earliest achievable time per fact.
children.body: The temporal pruned pass can evaluate through a time-gated build (0.23 Phase 4 probe 2): fact_time and op_time ride the same fused loop in build_rpg, END fires anchored at start + lag, and trpg_admit rejects ops whose earliest time would fall outside a TrpgWindow. It is armed only by the presence of the task.trpg table (built by the temporal path under FF_TRPG), and only relaxed_helpful can reach it — relaxed_to is always time-blind — so the complete temporal passes and every classical caller run the historical bytes. Included here for completeness; it belongs to the temporal mode's story.

children.title: Action costs (costs.rs)
children.summary: IPC-6 :action-costs on the classical path: detect the metric, replay its value, and polish the first plan with a bounded cost sweep.
children.body: Ferroplan's numeric machinery already tracks a cost fluent through grounding and apply; costs.rs makes the classical path reason about it. Three pieces: detection/replay, the cost-augmented relaxed plan in heuristic.rs, and the anytime improvement sweep. The optimal mode prices costs separately (optimal::op_costs, per-op constants only).

children.title: Metric detection and replay
children.summary: metric_fluent recognises minimize(single fluent); plan_cost replays a plan to read its true final value.
children.body: IPC-2008 action costs are a numeric fluent (conventionally total-cost) increased by constants and minimized by the metric. metric_fluent detects exactly the supported shape — minimize of a single ground fluent — and names it for PackedTask::fluent_id. plan_cost replays the op sequence through apply and reads the fluent: the same number VAL will compute. Every reported cost in the classical path goes through this replay; the sweep's own bound arithmetic is never trusted for the report.

children.title: Cost-augmented h (relaxed_costed)
children.summary: Relaxed-plan length plus the summed cost increases of the selected ops, so search prefers cheap achievers but keeps a gradient over free regions.
children.body:
relaxed_costed = relaxed_to count + selected_increase_sum toward the cost fluent, each op counted once (set semantics) and its increase evaluated in the current state. The "cost + 1 per action" shape is deliberate: a pure-cost h flatlines wherever the remaining actions are free. Not admissible (hFF underneath); an underestimate when a plan must repeat an op. relaxed_plan_cost returns the cost part alone, used by the PDDL3 forgo-aware seed.

Selected via SearchCfg::h_cost = Some(cf) (with_cost_h). The extraction still picks achievers by layer, not by cost — cost only enters the count.

children.title: Anytime cost sweep (improve)
children.summary: After the first plan, a bounded branch-and-bound best-first under its cost, ordered by g-cost and guided by cost-h, keeps the cheapest incumbent.
children.body:
The first plan comes from the untouched ladder, so cost support can never regress coverage. improve then runs search_from with cost_bound = first_cost, w_c = 1.0 (accumulated cost in the key), h_cost = cf, and anytime = true (tighten the bound in place on each accepting state and keep draining). The visited key appends the cost fluent so equal-fact/different-cost states stay distinct; under an orbit map it is appended after canonicalization.

Budget: sweep_budget = min(remaining eval budget, max(2 × solve evals, 30,000)); FF_COST_SWEEP_EVALS overrides, 0 disables. Un-capped exhaustion under the bound sets proven, and api.rs writes "plan cost proven optimal" into the notes.

children.title: Length sweep (opt-in negative)
children.summary: Iterated weights 3, 2, 1 with g_bound = incumbent length. ~1.8% shorter at ~28x the evals; default off.
children.body: improve_length restarts best-first at w_h = 3, 2, 1, each bounded by g_bound = best.len() (LAMA's restart-with-bound recipe). Budget comes only from FF_LEN_SWEEP_EVALS, default 0. STATUS.md and the book record the verdict: about 1.8% shorter plans at about 28× the evaluations, zero gain at proportionate budgets. The within-search alternative (FF_LEN_ANYTIME, SearchCfg::len_anytime) is also opt-in after costing 9 instances of coverage at 60 s.

children.title: Landmarks (landmarks.rs)
children.summary: 95 lines: classic delete-relaxation fact landmarks, consumed as LAMA's landmark-count signal.
children.body: A deliberately small module: one fixpoint RPG build and a backchaining queue, O(n_facts) memory, no quadratic per-fact landmark table. Added in the 0.9 roadmap Phase 3 as LAMA's backbone. Its value is as a second signal next to hFF.

children.title: First-achiever backchaining
children.summary: A fact common to the preconditions of every first achiever of a landmark is itself a landmark.
children.body:
Idea. A fact landmark is a fact every plan must make true at some point. Goals are trivial landmarks. If f is a landmark not true now, every plan uses one of f's first achievers (ops adding f whose op layer precedes f's fact layer in the relaxed graph); so any fact in the intersection of all their preconditions must also be reached first. Repeat to a fixpoint (Hoffmann, Porteous and Sebastia).

In ferroplan. landmarks_for(task, start, goal_pos) calls reachability_layers once (one fixpoint RPG build), seeds a queue with reachable goals, and for each queued fact intersects the first achievers' pre_pos (early exit when the intersection empties). Landmarks already true at start are dropped so the count means "necessary facts not yet made true". Output is a sorted Vec<u32> of fact ids. goal_landmarks is the init-state form. No orderings, no disjunctive landmarks, no action landmarks.

children.title: Landmark-count heuristic
children.summary: Path-dependent: landmarks not yet accepted on the path to a node. Per-node accepted bitset.
children.body:
The count is path-dependent, not a function of the state: a landmark is accepted once any state on the path made it true, and stays accepted. Each node carries an accepted bitset over the landmark list index (not fact ids); accept_into ORs in the landmarks the new state holds and unaccepted popcounts the remainder. Inadmissible as used (no cost partitioning, no re-required landmarks), but it keeps a progress gradient across exactly the plateaus where hFF goes flat: parking, floortile, barman, tidybot are named in lama.rs.

Two consumers with the same arithmetic: the LAMA rung (key 2·hFF + 4·lm) and the enriched best-first fallback (w_lm = 3.0 × 256 by default since 0.26 F1, via clm_accept_into/clm_unaccepted). Memory: ceil(n_lm/64) words per node, which the fallback's node-cap model charges explicitly.

children.title: Per-subgoal landmarks
children.summary: Landmarks recomputed for each (start, subgoal) pair so the partition cascade's LAMA stays sound.
children.body: landmarks_for takes an arbitrary start state and goal subset. The partition-and-resolve cascade (resolve::solve) solves subgoals from evolving states and calls lama::search_subgoal, which recomputes landmarks for exactly that piece; reusing the whole-task set would count landmarks irrelevant to the subgoal. The same is true of the fallback's w_lm term, computed per search_from call for its (start, goal).

children.title: Novelty / width measure
children.summary: A state is novel if it makes true some atom (or atom pair) no earlier state in its partition cell has. Ordering, not distance.
children.body:
Idea. Width-based search (Lipovetzky and Geffner): the novelty of a state is the size of the smallest tuple of atoms it makes true for the first time. IW(1) prunes every state of novelty > 1; BFWS uses novelty as the leading term of a best-first key and keeps the rest. Partitioning the "seen" tables by a coarse function (goals achieved, relaxed-plan progress) makes the measure local. Novelty is not a distance estimate and has no admissibility notion; it costs a bitset OR per state, far below hFF.

In ferroplan (novelty.rs): Seen::novel_and_mark keeps one seen-fact bitset per cell (u16, u16), lazily allocated, and returns whether bits & !seen != 0 while ORing the state in. Cells are ⟨unachieved goals⟩ (kept coarse on purpose: partitioning by parent h too made nearly every state novel and degenerated to plain greedy — the catalog-consume fixture's 895-step plan) or, in the driver, ⟨unachieved goals, achieved-R count⟩. Width 2 in the driver is tracked over pairs of R facts only (R ≤ 256 facts, so ≤ 4 KB of pair bits per cell). FF_NUMNOV=1 adds per-fluent seen-envelopes for fluent-only progress (sailing's one-predicate states).

children.title: Admissible heuristics (optimal.rs)
children.summary: h^max, LM-cut and incremental LM-cut over a conditional-effect-aware relaxation graph, maxed with the numeric layer bound.
children.body: The optimal mode has its own heuristic stack, independent of heuristic.rs except for the numeric layer bound. AstarState::eval chooses: incremental LM-cut, plain LM-cut, rep-folded hmax, or plain hmax; then maxes in fold_goal_bound or admissible_goal_layers where armed. Pattern databases (pdb.rs) and a variable cover (vars.rs) are described in docs/roadmap-0.31.md Lane C as built on the engine-0.31 branch; they are not in this tree.

children.title: RelaxGraph and costs
children.summary: Achievers built once per solve: one per op plus one per conditional effect, with sorted deduped preconditions.
children.body:
RelaxGraph::new builds an Achiever { op, pre, add } for each op and one extra per conditional effect whose pre is the op's preconditions plus the effect condition. This is the 0.20 admissibility repair: 0.19's hmax iterated only unconditional adds, so a goal reachable only through a (when ...) was labelled unreachable and A* certified wrong optima (the fixture in tests/optimal.rs pins "PROVEN cost 100" against a true optimum of 11). Indexes: by_pre, by_add, pre_free.

op_costs gives per-op constants: unit cost without a metric, else the sum of (increase (total-cost) c) effects; any state-dependent or non-increase cost rejects the problem from optimal mode with a named note. Numeric preconditions are dropped (a relaxation, so lower bounds survive).

children.title: h^max
children.summary: Cost of the most expensive goal fact, where each fact costs its cheapest achiever's max-precondition cost plus op cost. Dijkstra over facts.
children.body:
Idea. In the relaxed task, a fact's cost is the minimum over achievers of (op cost + the max of its preconditions' costs); hmax is the max over goal facts. It is admissible and consistent but weak, since it charges only the single hardest chain.

In ferroplan. hmax_labels is a Dijkstra with per-achiever unsatisfied-precondition counters (CutSpace::counts): an achiever fires when its last precondition settles, at label = that precondition's label + cost. O(edges · log facts) per call. With use_floors, rep-folded numeric floors raise an achiever's firing label (0.23 Phase 5 rung 2, NumFold). hmax wraps it. Role: the cheap "sprint" heuristic of the optimal ladder, and the whole of it when LM-cut is not informative at the root.

children.title: LM-cut
children.summary: Repeatedly find a cut of ops every relaxed plan must cross, charge its min cost, subtract it, re-run h^max; sum the charges.
children.body:
Idea (Helmert and Domshlak 2009). Compute hmax; with each achiever's precondition-choice function (its max-label precondition) build a justification graph; the ops crossing from the "before" zone into the goal zone form a disjunctive action landmark. Charge the cut's minimum cost, subtract it from every member, repeat until hmax reaches 0. The sum is a cost partitioning over landmarks, hence admissible, and usually much tighter than hmax; it is not consistent, so A* re-opens.

In ferroplan. lmcut → lmcut_rounds on a reusable CutSpace (label, cost, pcf, goal_zone, before, in_cut, ...). Each round zeroes at least one op, so the loop is bounded by n_ops + 1. Cost: one hmax label pass per round, often tens of passes per state — the expensive end of the table.

children.title: Incremental LM-cut
children.summary: A child inherits its parent's cuts minus those containing the op just applied, then continues LM-cut on residual costs.
children.body: The inheritance theorem in charge_cuts' doc: a disjunctive action landmark L of the relaxation from s stays one from s' = res(s, o) whenever o ∉ L, because any relaxed plan from s' prefixed with o is a relaxed plan from s and must hit L inside the suffix. So a child replays the parent's cut list in discovery order, charging each the min residual cost, then lmcut_rounds continues under those residual costs. Lists are capped (INC_CUT_CAP = 96 cuts, INC_LIST_CAP = 1024 words, about 4 KB per node worst case); truncation is never unsound. The saved label passes are counted in labels_computed. FF_NO_INC_LMCUT=1 restores the one-shot probe.

children.title: Extra ordering terms in the key
children.summary: Besides g and h, the best-first key can add landmark count, resource trips, metric cost, preference penalties and op penalties.
children.body:
SearchCfg documents the key units: one h unit = 1280 (5·256), one g step = 256, one unsatisfied preference = weight·100, one metric-cost unit = w_c·256. Optional terms, each defaulting to absent (key bit-identical):

  • w_lm × unaccepted landmarks — on by default in the plain classical fallback (3.0).
  • w_res × ⌈unmet linked goals / pool capacity⌉ — resource-trip bound from resource::TripBound, opt-in FF_RESLM.
  • w_c × accumulated metric cost — the cost sweep and preference B&B.
  • SatGuidance::penalty — forgone preference weight on the concrete state, a squared occupancy penalty for renewable resources, and ESPC locked-loss deadline terms; all things the delete relaxation cannot see.
  • a per-op penalty table scoped by with_op_penalty (0.29 Lane 1), so the PDDL3 polish prefers plans breaking the fewest held preferences.

title: Search strategies
summary: How states are explored: enforced hill-climbing, batched weighted best-first, LAMA, novelty/BFWS, A* for optimality, SAT, symmetry, and the ladder and portfolio that sequence them.
body: The satisficing story is a ladder of increasingly complete searches, each a bounded bet on a different signal, ending in a complete best-first. All open-list searches share three conventions: deferred evaluation (queue with the parent's h), fixed-size batches evaluated in parallel with order-preserving maps (plans identical at any thread count), and budgets counted in evaluated states and checked against a declared wall. The optimal and SAT modes are separate engines with stricter honesty rules: a plan with a certificate, or a named reason why not.

children.title: Which search runs when
children.summary: Mode selects the engine: auto/ff use the ladder, portfolio, partition, optimal and sat are explicit.
children.body:
ModeEngineComplete?

--search bfsenriched best-first onlyYes

Brackets mark rungs that are default-on only when FF_TIME_LIMIT is declared. The partition rung ahead of the ladder is opt-in (FF_PARTITION_RUNG=1).

children.title: The ladder (plan_avoiding)
children.summary: The default classical route: EHC, then bounded rungs, then the complete best-first, each rung entered only if the wall still affords it.
children.body:
search::plan → plan_avoiding is "the ladder" the roadmaps refer to. Each bounded rung is a bet that costs wall time before the complete fallback gets its turn. The record names that tax three times over: the 0.17 novelty rung (+7 / −51 budget-edge rows), the 0.28 seed-ladder tightening, and 0.30's partition rung (−26).

Affordability gate (0.18, refined 0.22 and 0.30): with FF_TIME_LIMIT declared, a bounded rung is entered only while more than 40% of the wall remains, re-read at each rung's entry (rungs_affordable); against the handed base when the partition rung handed down. With no limit set every rung runs and the ladder is byte-identical to its pre-0.18 form. Each rung also runs under its own wall slice (rung_slice), a deadline rather than a converted eval count because evals/s spans orders of magnitude.

What 0.31 plans (docs/roadmap-0.31.md Lane A): replace the hand-set fractions with a slice table learned from a per-rung matrix (FF_RUNG_ONLY, FF_LADDER_TABLE, ladder.rs), greedy most-coverage-per-second in the Stone Soup / Cedalion style, refereed leave-one-domain-out. None of that is in this tree yet. Probe hatches today: FF_NOVELTY_ONLY, FF_NOVLIGHT_ONLY, FF_NOVDRIVER_ONLY; narration via FF_WALL_DEBUG. Fixtures: tests/ladder_wall.rs, tests/novdriver.rs, tests/refill.rs.

children.title: 0. Partition rung (opt-in)
children.summary: FF_PARTITION_RUNG=1: partition-and-resolve under half the wall before the ladder. Measured out of the default in 0.30.
children.body: In api.rs, in auto mode with a wall of at least 10 s, never on a constrained task: invariants::synthesize + resolve::solve under tighten_deadline leaving 1 − FF_PARTITION_RUNG_FRAC (0.5). On hand-down it calls search::hand_ladder_wall(left) so the ladder's affordability gate is judged against what it was handed. The 0.30 Lane 6 board read: +6 pathways cells against −26 first-attempt on cells the ladder solves late, so it ships opt-in only.

children.title: 1. EHC
children.summary: Always first when ehc_first; solves most instances. Hands down on plateau, eval cap or wall slice.
children.body: Entered unless the caller asked for --search bfs. Under a declared wall it gets 0.25 of the remaining wall, extended on progress up to 0.6. A success returns ehc_fell_back: false; every later rung's success is reported as a fallback.

children.title: 2. Novelty-light
children.summary: IW(1)-style, goal-count guided, zero h evaluations. Default-on only under a declared affordable wall.
children.body: novelty::search_light, capped at NOVLIGHT_CAP = 300,000 pops and FF_NOVLIGHT_WALL_FRAC (0.10) of the remaining wall. Placed before LAMA because its tax is small by construction (a pop is successor generation plus a bitset OR) and the width-y shapes EHC dies on are where it wins: visit-all-2014 receipts at 899/3135/3248 pops. FF_NOVLIGHT=1 forces it, FF_NO_NOVLIGHT=1 opts out.

children.title: 3. LAMA rung
children.summary: Bounded landmark + preferred-op greedy search, 400k evals and 0.25 of the remaining wall. Default-on.
children.body: lama::search(task, threads, LAMA_CAP.min(max_eval), forbidden, slice) with LAMA_CAP = 400,000 and a slice of FF_LAMA_WALL_FRAC (0.25) of the remaining wall (folded with any per-call deadline by sooner_deadline). It runs where EHC gave up, i.e. where the relaxed plan has plateaued. FF_NO_LAMA=1 removes it.

children.title: 4. Novelty driver (BFWS-like)
children.summary: The h-free partitioned width-2 driver, 400k evals and half the remaining wall. Default-on under a declared wall.
children.body: novelty::search_driver with NOVELTY_CAP = 400,000 and FF_NOV_WALL_FRAC (0.50 since 0.26 F3, where every transport conversion on 2008/2011 was the driver's). It replaced the 0.17 h-guided novelty rung at this slot in 0.22; FF_NOV_OLD=1 swaps the old rung back. As the last bounded rung it gets the biggest slice: everything behind it is the complete fallback.

children.title: 5. Enriched weighted best-first
children.summary: search_from at 1·g + 5·h with preferred-op alternation and the landmark term; the complete backstop.
children.body: Before entering, plan_avoiding sets pref_ops and w_lm = 3.0 unless FF_NO_ENRICH, applies FF_CLM/FF_RESLM overrides and optional FF_LEN_ANYTIME. A plan returns with ehc_fell_back = ehc_first, which api.rs turns into the note "EHC found no improving state; used weighted best-first".

children.title: 6. Refill rounds
children.summary: If the fallback was capped (not exhausted) with >10% of a declared wall left, re-enter greedier: w_h x4, max_eval x4, up to 6 times.
children.body: 0.20 Phase 1 "spend the whole wall": the tpp-numeric witness had the fallback cap at 7.8 s and hand back 25 s of a 60 s wall. Genuine exhaustion returns at once (completeness does not depend on weight). If the round died on the node cap rather than the eval cap, the byte target doubles too, at most ×4 total (0.22 Phase 2, sailing-wind), narrated ungated on stderr so a later RSS kill can be named self-inflicted. Disarmed by an explicit eval cap (a budgeted-think contract) or FF_NO_REFILL=1; without a wall it is a single round.

children.title: search.rs: best-first, EHC, the ladder
children.summary: 2,629 lines: the data-parallel weighted best-first engine, enforced hill-climbing, budgets, and plan_avoiding (the ladder).
children.body: The core satisficing engine. search_from is the reusable best-first; ehc/bfs_improve are FF's hill-climber; plan/plan_avoiding compose them with the other rungs into the ladder; solve_subgoal* expose the engine to partition-and-resolve. Most of the file's volume is budget machinery: wall slices, node caps, refill rounds and hatches, each with its measurement in the comments.

children.title: SearchCfg and the 1·g + 5·h key
children.summary: Integer heap key w_g·g + w_h·h with weights pre-scaled by 256; the default 1·g + 5·h is weighted A* leaning greedy.
children.body:
SearchCfg::from_weights(1.0, 5.0, None) is the default: w_g = 256, w_h = 1280 (WEIGHT_SCALE = 256), so fractional weights are possible while the historical key stays bit-identical. Inputs are sanitized: non-finite or negative weights fall back to the default, weights clamp to 1e9, both-zero restores defaults (an all-zero key would degrade to insertion order). max_eval defaults to DEFAULT_MAX_EVAL = 5,000,000 evaluated states.

The struct also carries every per-search mode switch: h_cost, w_c, anytime, g_bound, len_anytime, w_lm, w_res, pref_ops, node_bytes_target, deadline, ehc_wall_frac. Each field's doc records the cycle that added it and its measured verdict, a pattern used throughout the crate.

children.title: Weighted best-first (search_from)
children.summary: The complete fallback: batched best-first over a binary heap with hash-based dedup, node cap, wall checkpoints and orbit-canonical keys.
children.body:
search_from is the generic engine. It checks the initial state for a relaxed dead end, computes landmarks if w_lm > 0, sizes the node cap, and loops: pop a batch, goal-check, evaluate h in parallel, expand in parallel, then insert serially. The open list is BinaryHeap<Reverse<(i64, usize)>>; ties break on node index, i.e. insertion order.

Dedup: visited maps a 64-bit state-key hash to the node indices with that hash (0.20 Phase 4 retained-state compression — no second copy of the bitset), and state_key_eq decides collisions. The key excludes irrelevant fluents (termination) and, under branch-and-bound, appends the cost fluent. With an orbit map, the hash is canonical_skey_hash; the orbit is dropped whenever a forbidden mask, preference guidance or closure is in play.

It serves the ladder's fallback, the portfolio's bfs members, the cost sweep, the length sweep, the PDDL3 B&B loops (SatGuidance, ClosureCost, anytime) and the solve_subgoal* family used by partition-and-resolve.

children.title: Deferred (lazy) evaluation
children.summary: A successor is queued with its parent's h; its own h is computed only when popped. Many inserted nodes are never evaluated.
children.body:
Idea. Eager best-first evaluates every generated successor; deferred evaluation (Fast Downward's "lazy" search) evaluates a node only when it is expanded and orders the open list by the parent's value. With high branching factors this cuts heuristic calls by a large factor at the cost of a less accurate ordering.

In ferroplan all three heap searches use it: in search_from successors carry the parent's h as their key (comment at the heap declaration); LAMA and the novelty rungs do the same. Since 0.30 Lane 5 the LAMA rung and the novelty driver go further with a lazy frontier: an open entry is only (key, father, op) and the state is regenerated from the father on pop, because on city-car i6 the LAMA rung held 3.2–3.4 GB in generated successors it never evaluated. STATUS.md notes that LAMA's own lazy evaluation "was deliberately skipped — batch-parallel eval is ferroplan's answer"; the deferred keying here is that batch scheme, not FD's one-at-a-time lazy loop.

children.title: Parallel batch evaluation
children.summary: Pop a fixed batch, evaluate h with an order-preserving parallel map, insert serially: identical plans at any thread count.
children.body:
Each round pops up to BATCH = 256 nodes (or 192 + 64 from the two heaps under pref_ops). h for the whole batch runs through par::par_map_with(&popped, threads, || Scratch::new(task), ...); successor generation for live nodes runs through par::par_map. Both preserve input order and all control flow — goal checks, dedup, heap pushes, caps — happens on the calling thread. So the module doc's contract holds: "the plan found is identical regardless of the worker count — only the wall-clock of heuristic evaluation changes". Tests check t1 ≡ t8.

Wall checks: one clock read per batch normally; under an armed deadline each evaluation reads the clock first (the 0.28 Lane I in-batch checkpoint, because at 8 ms per eval a 256-batch is two seconds), and a tripped batch returns capped without using its h values.

children.title: Preferred-op alternation in the fallback
children.summary: 0.26 F1: the plain classical fallback evaluates with relaxed_helpful and pops 192 from a preferred heap and 64 from the normal heap each round.
children.body: With cfg.pref_ops, a successor reached through a parent's helpful op sits in both heaps; an expanded flag makes it expand once. Every key is computed exactly as before and the normal heap still holds everything, so open-list exhaustion still means exhaustion — only pop order changes. Together with w_lm = 3.0 this is "the LAMA recipe transplanted" onto the rung that writes "EHC found no improving state; used weighted best-first" (128 of ipc5-prop's 369 solved rows when added). Scoped to plan_avoiding's plain classical fallback only; FF_NO_ENRICH=1 restores the single heap.

children.title: Enforced hill-climbing
children.summary: From the current state, breadth-first over helpful actions only until a strictly better h appears; jump there and repeat. Fast, incomplete.
children.body:
Idea (FF, Hoffmann 2001). Greedy local search: commit to the first state with strictly lower h found by a breadth-first lookahead, so plateaus are crossed by exhaustive local search. Restricting the lookahead to helpful actions makes it fast and incomplete; FF falls back to complete best-first when it fails.

In ferroplan. ehc loops bfs_improve, a BFS from the current state expanding only each node's helpful ops, deduped by StateKey, capped at BFS_CAP = 5,000 expansions per lookahead. Total budget (200 · n_ops).max(30,000).min(max_eval) evaluations — the op-count scaling took gripper-250 from 2.16M evals / 33 s to 32k / 0.86 s (docs/perf-notes.md). Under an armed wall, a deadline slice of FF_EHC_WALL_FRAC (0.25) of the remaining wall is checked per evaluation; since 0.29 Lane W the slice restarts on each improvement, under a ceiling of FF_EHC_WALL_MAX_FRAC (0.6). Single-threaded and deterministic. Plans are valid but not length-optimal.

children.title: Caps, deadlines and the memory wall
children.summary: Node caps from a byte model, per-call deadlines, a teardown reserve, and a measured RSS wall shape every search's exit.
children.body: node_cap_for converts a retained-bytes target (8 GiB on 64-bit, 2 GiB on 32-bit, overridden by FF_MEM_BUDGET_GB or the rlimit) into a node count with per_node_model_bytes; FF_SEARCH_NODE_CAP sets it directly. crate::mem::MemWall reads the process's real resident size once per batch and trips like a cap. Wall time: FF_TIME_LIMIT arms a process clock (arm_wall_limit), SearchCfg::deadline and the thread-local CallBudget carry per-call deadlines and cancel flags, reserve_for_report holds back seconds so a found plan is reported before a runner kills at the wall. A capped return is PlanResult::Unsolvable { capped: true } and is never reported as "proven unsolvable".

children.title: LAMA rung (lama.rs)
children.summary: Greedy best-first over h_FF and landmark count with preferred-operator boosting: the rung for long goal-interaction plateaus.
children.body: Why a separate rung (module doc): EHC and plain weighted best-first die where the relaxed plan plateaus on long goal-interaction chains (parking, floortile, barman, tidybot). Landmarks not yet achieved keep a gradient across those plateaus and helpful-action boosting keeps branching near the relaxed plan's. It runs bounded, after EHC and before the complete fallback, so on its own it can only add coverage; the wall it spends is the cost. Barman11 went to 20/20 with it (STATUS.md). FF_TLAMA is a temporal variant, measured negative.

children.title: Key and dual open lists
children.summary: Greedy key 2·h_FF + 4·landmarks (no g); preferred heap and normal heap, 192 + 64 pops per round.
children.body:
The priority key is W_FF · h + W_LM · lm with W_FF = 2 and W_LM = 4, using the parent's h (deferred) and the child's unaccepted landmark count. There is no g term: it is pure greedy, as LAMA's first iteration is. Successors reached via one of the parent's helpful ops go on both pref_heap and norm_heap; each round pops PREF_BATCH = 192 preferred and NORM_BATCH = 64 normal entries. Evaluation of the popped batch uses relaxed_helpful in an order-preserving parallel map; insertion is serial. Plans are identical at any thread count.

Difference from LAMA proper: no landmark orderings or reasonable orderings, no action costs in the key, no restarting weighted A* iterations; length anytime only behind FF_LEN_ANYTIME.

children.title: Lazy frontier
children.summary: Open entries are (key, father, op); states are regenerated from the father on pop and closed by 128-bit key hash.
children.body: Since 0.30 Lane 5, nodes holds only popped (closed) states. keys: FxHashMap<u128, u32> maps a state-key hash to its closed index, or OPEN (u32::MAX) while it is only on a heap. A hash seen at generation is a duplicate; a hash already closed at pop time is the other heap's copy. The rung instruments false_drops (hash duplicates whose closed twin is a different state) on the half that can be checked. MemWall::arm_rung adds a measured RSS trip per batch because the modelled node cap under-charges this rung's per-node accepted bitsets.

children.title: Window extension (arrival test)
children.summary: An opt-in rule to extend the rung's wall slice only while its demonstrated pace can reach key 0 inside the remaining wall.
children.body: extend_window(key_now, key_drop, affordable_windows) extends only if key_now ≤ EXT_OPTIMISM · key_drop · affordable_windows with EXT_OPTIMISM = 4. A stalled or regressing window never extends. The constant was priced on two measured shapes: spider p01 (key 584, drop 58, affordable 4) needs ≥ 2.52, and nurikabe i12 (key 496, drop 20, affordable 4) tolerates < 6.2. Later windows cross, which is why the code says the rule is opt-in rather than default. Unit tests pin both shapes.

children.title: search_subgoal
children.summary: The same rung over an arbitrary start state and subgoal, with landmarks recomputed for that pair; used by the partition cascade.
children.body: lama::search is a thin wrapper over search_subgoal(task, &init, goal_pos, goal_num, ...). resolve::solve calls the subgoal form per partition piece. The portfolio and partition cascade pass slice = None (their budget discipline is their own); the ladder passes its FF_LAMA_WALL_FRAC slice.

children.title: Novelty rungs (novelty.rs)
children.summary: Width-based search in three forms: novelty-light (IW(1), h-free), the partitioned width-2 driver, and the older h-guided rung.
children.body: Where the relaxed plan's gradient is wrong or exhausted, novelty-first exploration visits structurally new states without asking h. The modern IPC corpora (2018/2023) are full of those domains and every winner there has a novelty component (docs/landscape-2026.md, cited in the module doc). All three searches share the rung contracts: bounded by eval cap + node cap + measured memory wall, wall-sliced under a declared budget, deterministic.

children.title: search_light: IW(1) + goal count
children.summary: Key ⟨novel, unachieved goals, insertion⟩, single serial heap, zero h calls, flat arena.
children.body: Added in 0.20 Phase 3 after the scoping probe found the h-guided rung solved visit-all-2014 i1 but spent 35 s of wall entirely inside per-pop relaxed_helpful. A pop here costs successor generation and a bitset OR. No dead-end pruning (nothing computes ∞); the pop cap and node cap are the exits. Since the 0.30 cut, states live in three flat arrays (a_bits, a_fv, a_fdef) with father/op arrays and chained dedup buckets: ~88 bytes a node against ~340, which let LAMA enter woodworking i15 at 2.17 GiB instead of tripping the memory wall (tests/novlight_arena.rs). Serial, deterministic.

children.title: search_driver: partitioned width-2
children.summary: One root relaxed plan builds R; key ⟨rank novel-1 < novel-2 < non-novel, #g, |R|−r⟩; h-free per pop.
children.body:
0.22 Phase 5B lever 3, after the parking receipt (86 s of cumulative worker time building h per pop at 100k evals). r_partition_facts takes the goal facts plus the root extraction's need-facts (extraction_need_facts), capped at r_cap = 256 lowest-fact-layer first. Cells are ⟨unachieved goals, achieved-R count⟩; width 2 is tracked over R-pairs via a triangular index (tri). One heuristic call in total. Wall: the slice and wall_hard_expired checked every 4,096 pops. DriverCfg::from_env: FF_NOV_PART=0, FF_NOV_W2=0, FF_NOV_R_CAP.

docs/roadmap-0.31.md reads this as BFWS(f5) "in all but name" and lists what the IPC winners have beyond it: Dual BFWS's pruned front end, novelty-first LAMA (f6), R recomputed on progress, and forgetting (Scorpion Maidu). Those are Lane B plans, not code here.

children.title: search: h-guided novelty (0.17)
children.summary: Novelty first, then goal count, then parent h, with dual heaps and parallel relaxed_helpful. Kept behind FF_NOV_OLD.
children.body: The original rung: key weights W_NOVEL = 240 and W_GOALS = 220 keep novelty dominant, then goal count, then parent h; preferred/normal heaps with 192/64 pops; parallel h. The 0.17 referee measured +7 / −51 against the default ladder because of its wall tax ahead of the fallback, and made it opt-in; the 0.18 budget gate turned the arithmetic to +4 / −0, and the 0.22 driver then replaced it in the ladder. FF_NOVELTY_ONLY=1 probes it alone.

children.title: Numeric novelty (FF_NUMNOV)
children.summary: Opt-in per-cell seen-envelopes over quantized relevant fluent values, for tasks whose progress is fluent-only.
children.body: Bit tables are blind on fluent-only progress (sailing has one predicate, so every successor is bit-identical). Under FF_NUMNOV=1 on a task with relevant fluents, each cell also keeps a (min, max) envelope per relevant fluent over the 1e-6-quantized values from packed.rs's state-key quantizer; leaving the envelope counts as novel. Off, num_cells is None and it costs nothing.

children.title: Optimal search (optimal.rs)
children.summary: Sequential-optimal planning: resumable A* with LM-cut / h^max, a wall-aware sprint-and-probe ladder, numeric arms, orbit dedup.
children.body: Added in 0.19, LM-cut and the conditional-effect admissibility repair in 0.20, resumable engine 0.22, incremental LM-cut 0.23. It shares the packed task with every other mode and builds its own relaxation graph. The heuristics themselves are described under Heuristics → Admissible. docs/roadmap-0.31.md Lane C notes that 42% of unsolved rows are on optimal tracks, where the engine has "one admissible heuristic"; PDBs and cost partitioning are that lane's plan.

children.title: Scope: proof or nothing
children.summary: Mode::Optimal returns a plan only with an optimality certificate; caps and wall return INCONCLUSIVE.
children.body: Explicit only (--mode optimal); auto never routes here. Costs are per-op constants; state-dependent costs reject with a named note. Numeric preconditions and goals are exact in expansion and the goal test and ignored or soundly bounded in h. A node cap or wall trip returns OptOutcome with proven = false — never a best-effort incumbent. The 0.30.0 standings report 694 certified optima across the boards (README).

children.title: Resumable A* engine
children.summary: AstarState keeps open list, arena and best_g across runs so a later run continues instead of re-treading; re-opens because LM-cut is inconsistent.
children.body: AstarState (0.22 Phase 3) is one A* whose state survives the return of run(max_nodes, deadline). Soundness of resume rides pending: a trip happens after a pop, so the tripped node is parked and its successor loop re-driven first on the next run. With an admissible h and re-opening via best_g, the first goal pop is optimal across resumes. f-ties break on lower h, then insertion order; search is serial. Visited keys go through OrbitMap::canonical_skey when an orbit is present; under FF_ORBIT_ISO goal tests use the relaxed witness and the plan is remapped.

children.title: The optimal ladder (solve)
children.summary: Root gate compares h^max and LM-cut; h^max sprints, an incremental LM-cut probe follows, h^max resumes, then a second probe round.
children.body:
solve under a declared wall:

  1. Root gate: compute hmax and LM-cut at the initial state. If LM-cut is not more informative by a ratio ≥ FF_OPT_GATE_MARGIN (1.4), hmax A* holds the whole wall (astar_wall_refill).
  2. hmax sprint with max_nodes/4 and FF_OPT_SPRINT_FRAC (0.4) of the wall, or 0.1 when the ratio is ≥ 2.
  3. Incremental LM-cut probe: max_nodes/2, FF_OPT_LMCUT_PROBE_FRAC (0.33) of the remaining wall.
  4. hmax resumes its open list; on a node-cap exit with >10% wall left the cap doubles in place.
  5. Round 2: the probe engine resumes with a doubled budget if wall remains.

Without a wall: a quarter-budget hmax pass, then full LM-cut. Hatches: FF_NO_LMCUT, FF_NO_HMAX_SPRINT, FF_OPT_NO_ROOTGATE, FF_OPT_NO_RESUME, FF_NO_INC_LMCUT.

children.title: Numeric arms
children.summary: Rep-folded h^max floors and the audited RPG layer bound raise h on numeric tasks without losing admissibility.
children.body: Two arms, both maxed into h. num_arm_root gates the RPG layer bound (admissible_goal_layers, armed only when numeric_interval_audit passes). num_fold_prep builds a NumFold: per-achiever FoldMargins that give an admissible floor on the steps before an achiever's numeric conditions can hold, filled per state by fold_fill_floors and read by hmax_labels(use_floors = true); fold_goal_bound adds a goal-side bound. The fold arms only in unit-step currency and fails closed (fixture num_fold_gates_fail_closed_and_prices_p04_exactly).

children.title: Symmetry orbits (orbits.rs)
children.summary: Goal-respecting object-symmetry: states that differ only by permuting interchangeable objects collapse to one visited key.
children.body: Motivated by temporal-machine-shop being 0/20 (0.13 diagnosis): interchangeable pieces, distinguished only by which goal pair they serve, make every assignment of identical pieces a distinct visited state. The reduction canonicalizes visited keys under member relabeling; plans stay concrete. Soundness is conservative at every step; the module doc lists each bail condition. Ferroplan does orbit canonicalization of keys, not orbit search or symmetry-breaking constraints.

children.title: Detection: families and closure
children.summary: Find interchangeable member units, group every grounded display touching them into families, and verify closure under transpositions.
children.body: Candidates must have identical init profiles (statics and fluents), appear in no action schema literally, and pass a per-family closure check: within each equality-pattern class of member coordinates, cells are uniformly present or absent, so the grounded task really is closed under every member transposition. Every fact/op/fluent touching an orbit object joins a Family (shared head and literal/slot pattern) stored as a dense table over member coordinates (FamSet, CELL_CAP = 222), so a permutation acts on the whole task by table lookup — including cross-member facts like TMS's (assemble p q). Goals must be per-member and shared by the orbit; TILs, derived rules, PDDL3 constraints, numeric goals on touched fluents bail. A non-total-time metric bails unless op costs are uniform within each class (cost_uniform, the 0.22 L2 gate). Any violation drops detection entirely.

children.title: Canonical keys
children.summary: Pick σ by sorting per-member signatures, rewrite the visited key through the family tables; nodes stay concrete.
children.body: canonical_key (temporal: bits, relevant fluents and pending-end agenda ops permute together), canonical_skey and canonical_skey_hash (classical). The canonical form is a pure function of the state, so determinism and t1 ≡ t8 hold. Any σ is sound: canon(s1) = canon(s2) implies s2 is an automorphism image of s1; ties may miss merges but never mis-merge. Only visited keys are canonicalized; plan extraction and VAL see concrete states. The B&B cost fluent is appended after canonicalization.

children.title: Consumers and gates
children.summary: Temporal visited key (0.14), classical best-first dedup, partition passdown, cost sweep and optimal A* (0.22).
children.body: detect serves the temporal path. detect_classical (strict) feeds search_from's dedup, resolve::solve and costs::improve via api.rs; constrained tasks get no orbit. detect_classical_iso feeds optimal A*, the one classical consumer wired for the relaxed goal test. search_from drops the orbit whenever a forbidden mask, preference guidance or closure is in play, because a mask σ does not fix would break the automorphism. Hatches: FF_NO_ORBIT (all), FF_NO_ORBIT_CLASSICAL (classical only), FF_ORBIT_DEBUG.

children.title: Goal-isomorphism arm (opt-in)
children.summary: FF_ORBIT_ISO=1: orbits formed goal-blind; goals are tested up to a witness permutation and the plan is remapped.
children.body: 0.23 Phase 4 probe 1, default off. Units form on type and init profile only, so the goal never splits an orbit. Designated goal atoms (IsoGoal::desig) must be served by distinct members; the consumer must goal-test through iso_goal_witness (a backtracking search for a consistent σ, iso_bt) and remap emitted ops with iso_remap_op. Only optimal A* receives such maps. Flag off, every entry point is byte-identical to the strict detection.

children.title: Generation-side stabilizers (opt-in)
children.summary: FF_ORBIT_GEN: skip generating an op whose state-fixing member swap maps it to an already generated sibling.
children.body: stabilizer_classes computes the member classes the current state (and agenda) leaves fixed; gen_key maps an op to a class representative so siblings are generated once. Measured on TMS: 2.4× real evals at equal budget and duplicates 81% → 53%, but zero new solves, and the per-expansion stabilizer scan cost match-cellar 9 instances, so the 0.15 referee made it opt-in (book tuning.md).

children.title: SAT planning (sat.rs)
children.summary: The planner-side SAT wing: bounded-layer ∃-step encoding of the grounded task over the in-tree CDCL solver, with a horizon ramp and a temporal CEGAR face.
children.body: 0.24 Phases 2 and 3. This file is the encoder, ramp, decoder and STN teacher; the solver is the separate ferroplan-sat crate (Solver, Lit, ExtendFormula). Every plan is replay-verified; every non-plan outcome carries an honest note (declined, no plan within horizon H, or bounded-horizon UNSAT).

children.title: ∃-step encoding
children.summary: Each layer is a set of ops serializable in ascending op id; Rintanen-style disabling chains, effect and explanatory frame clauses.
children.body:
EncTask::build lays out fact variables per layer, op variables per layer and chain variables. Clauses: op ⇒ preconditions at layer entry; a per-fact linear accumulator over that fact's deleters in chain order, forbidding a member after an earlier member deleted its precondition; effect clauses pinning the exit state to the union of effects (an add/delete conflict on one fact is unsatisfiable); explanatory frames, so an empty layer copies its state and no noop ops are needed. Mutex groups from invariants.rs seed extra clauses. drop_twin_ops removes content-identical ops; encodability declines numeric, conditional effects, TILs and constraints with a named reason.

This is deliberately the incomplete-per-layer fragment of ∃-step (preconditions anchored at layer entry): it only prunes packings, never plans, since any plan fits one op per layer.

children.title: Horizon ramp and self-pricing
children.summary: Horizons 1, 2, 4 ... ≤ 128; each priced before encoding; ramp on UNSAT or budget trip; wall and conflict-rate bails.
children.body: ramp doubles h up to SatCfg::max_horizon (128). Before encoding, price(h) gives exact clause and literal counts; over price_cap (default 50M vars + literals, tightened by the remaining wall) it declines with a note rather than hang. solve_horizon spends conflicts_per_horizon (200,000) in 4,096-conflict slices so the wall check stays live, and bails if the conflict rate cannot finish the budget inside the slice. It ramps on budget exhaustion as well as UNSAT (avoiding the classic SATPLAN wait for UNSAT proofs at pre-goal horizons). Honesty rule: a trip is "no plan within horizon H", never "unsolvable". Knobs: FF_SAT_HORIZON, FF_SAT_CONFLICTS, FF_SAT_CAP.

children.title: Decode and replay
children.summary: Layers in order, ops in chain order, each replayed through PackedTask::apply with an applicability check; a miss is refused.
children.body: decode reads op variables per layer; replay executes the serialization from the initial state, checking applicability at every step and the goal at the end. Every emitted plan carries its own serialization proof; a replay failure is treated as an encoder bug (debug_assert, refused in release), never shipped.

children.title: Temporal face: STN-taught CEGAR
children.summary: Snap start/end events as layered actions, pairing clauses via RUNNING tokens, Bellman-Ford STN; negative cycles become refutation clauses.
children.body: Durations never enter the CNF. Snap tokens pair starts with ends; clauses forbid self-overlap, require all tokens false at the end, and enforce over-all invariants from the InvMap. The decoded event order goes to stn_schedule (longest-path Bellman-Ford). A positive cycle yields a pairing-guarded refutation clause (core_clause), re-solved inside the same horizon, at most MAX_REFUTATIONS_PER_HORIZON = 100. Reduced cores generalize across layer shifts and later horizons (0.25). Feasible schedules go through temporal::emit_scheduled and are validated against the original problem. Temporal auto arms it as a rung per temporal::solve's policy (FF_NO_SAT restores).

children.title: When SAT runs
children.summary: Classical: --mode sat, or auto under the FF_SAT_CLASSICAL smoke opt-in. Temporal: a rung on the temporal ladder.
children.body: api::solve_sat grounds, synthesizes mutex groups and calls solve_classical (or solve_temporal). In classical auto, SAT is reached only under FF_SAT_CLASSICAL, falling back to the classic path when SAT declines. It is not on the classical ladder. Useful where the plan is short and parallel but heuristic search plateaus (puzzle shapes).

children.title: Preference selection (selection.rs)
children.summary: Exact preference-subset selection for PDDL3 metrics: a small DFS branch-and-bound picks which preferences to target, then the planner plans to that target.
children.body:
Why. On zero-action-cost preference domains the score is decided by which jointly satisfiable preference subset the end state lands in; h-guided search cannot coordinate that (tpp p05: SGPlan5's score is the closed-form optimum of the selection; docs/forensics-tpp.md).

Model. One variable per invariant mutex group touched by a preference disjunct (domain = member facts in some disjunct plus ⊥), one boolean per ungrouped disjunct fact. A preference is satisfied iff some DNF disjunct (its P3COLLECT op's non-P3 precondition facts) is fully chosen. select minimizes violated weight by DFS branch-and-bound: variables by descending touched weight, values by descending immediately satisfied weight, prune on violated-so-far ≥ best, deterministic NODE_CAP = 200,000 keeping the best found.

Bound. The returned bound is admissible-optimistic (it ignores joint resource caps), so final metric = bound proves optimality. Caller: pddl3.rs (the closure optimizer), which plans the chosen facts as a hard target. FF_PREF_NO_SELECT=1 disables. It ties SGPlan5 on tpp p06 (book).

children.title: Portfolio (portfolio.rs)
children.summary: Mode::Portfolio: four complementary classical configs under one deterministic evaluation pool; ladder first, then doubling slices.
children.body: A sequential portfolio (ferroplan-roadmap Phase 6). Not to be confused with the ladder: the ladder is the default route and spends wall through slices; the portfolio is opt-in and spends evaluations, so its schedule is reproducible on any machine. docs/roadmap-0.31.md cites it as the existing "evaluation-budget portfolio" that its per-rung matrix will measure alongside the ladder rungs (FF_RUNG_ONLY=portfolio, planned).

children.title: Phase A: ladder on the full pool
children.summary: Member 'ladder' (plan with EHC) runs to its natural end on the whole eval budget first.
children.body: The settled Phase 6 verdict: the pure doubling schedule preempted the ladder and net-lost 11 corpus instances (sokoban −7, visit-all −4), gaining +2. Running the ladder first on the full pool makes portfolio coverage ≥ default by construction. If it returns a plan, the note reads portfolio: solved by member `ladder`. FF_PORTFOLIO_SLICED=1 skips this phase.

children.title: Doubling rounds over what is left
children.summary: Slices start at 50,000 evals and double each round; members run in fixed order ladder, lama, bfs-w3, bfs-w1.
children.body: Each round, every alive member gets min(SLICE0 << round, pool) evaluations. The pool is charged by each member's actual count (at least 1), so the schedule is in evaluated states, never wall clock — machine and thread independent. Members: ladder (EHC → LAMA → best-first), lama alone (plateau domains), bfs-w3 (weighted best-first at w_h = 3, no EHC detour), bfs-w1 (near-uniform).

children.title: Member retirement
children.summary: A member that used less than its slice without a plan hit an internal wall (node cap, dead end) and is retired.
children.body: If used < budget the member stopped for a reason a bigger slice cannot fix, so alive[m] = false. The LAMA member does not report evals on failure and is charged its whole slice. The loop ends when the pool is empty or no member is alive.

children.title: Settle: plan or proof
children.summary: First plan wins; an un-capped exhaustion by a complete bfs member proves the task unsolvable and ends the schedule.
children.body: Coverage first: the first plan any member finds is returned with the winner's name; cost and length polishing then run downstream on it as for any single config. A bfs member returning Unsolvable { capped: false } exhausted the space under no bound, so the whole task is settled unsolvable. The ladder member never claims a proof through the wrapper. Measured (STATUS.md, 580 IPC-2008/2011 instances at 60 s): extrapolated ~428 against the default's 427 after Phase A; it stays opt-in as --mode portfolio.
